module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gourevitch's series identity

*References:*
 - [About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series](https://doi.org/10.1080/10586458.2003.10504518) by *Jesús Guillera*
 - [G2003] Guillera, Jesús. "About a new kind of Ramanujan-type series." Experimental Mathematics 12.4 (2003): 507-510.
 - [A2025] Au, Kam Cheong. "Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities." Journal of Symbolic Computation 130 (2025): 102421. [arXiv:2312.14051](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14051)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Gourevitch


/-- The Gourevitch series identity:
The following identity holds:
$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1 + 14 n + 76 n^2 + 168 n^3}{2^{20 n}} \binom{2n}{n}^7 = \frac{32}{\pi^3}.$
This was originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera and proven in [A2025] by Au.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem gourevitch_series_identity :
    ∑' n : ℕ, ((1 + 14 * n + 76 * n ^ 2 + 168 * n ^ 3) / (2 ^ (20 * n)) : ℝ)
      * Nat.centralBinom n ^ 7 = 32 / (Real.pi ^ 3) := by
  sorry

end Gourevitch

findings.description: The docstring says the identity was "originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera." The cited paper instead credits Boris Gourevitch with discovering it and communicating it in 2002. This is an attribution error only; the Lean identity is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Guillera, "About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series," §4, p. 509, immediately before equation (4–1): "Boris Gourevitch [Gourevitch 02] has sent me, by email, the formula below for 1/π³. He has found it by using integer relations algorithms." The bibliography identifies [Gourevitch 02] as a 2002 personal communication. Full paper: https://emis.dsd.sztaki.hu/journals/EM/expmath/volumes/12/12.4/Guillera.pdf .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attribution sentence with: "This identity was discovered by Boris Gourevitch in 2002, reported by Guillera in [G2003], and proved by Au in [A2025]."

reformulations.difference: The sources write the summand using (1/2)ₙ⁷/(n!)⁷ and denominator 2^(6n), whereas Lean uses centralBinom(n)^7 and denominator 2^(20n). Lean also expresses the series identity as a `tsum` equality rather than explicitly asserting convergence of partial sums.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every n ≥ 0, (1/2)ₙ/n! = binom(2n,n)/4^n, so the source summand equals the Lean summand: 4^(7n)·2^(6n) = 2^(20n). The summands are nonnegative, making ordinary partial-sum convergence equivalent to Mathlib's unconditional `HasSum`. Finally, 32/π³ > 0, so the default value `tsum = 0` for a nonsummable series cannot satisfy this equality. Thus the bare `tsum` equality also asserts the required convergence. A sorry-free equivalence proof for the exact reviewed statement is in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

sources_consulted: Jesús Guillera, About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series, Experimental Mathematics 12(4) (2003), 507–510; entire paper, especially §4, equation (4–1): https://emis.dsd.sztaki.hu/journals/EM/expmath/volumes/12/12.4/Guillera.pdf
Kam Cheong Au, Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities, arXiv:2312.14051v4; LaTeX introduction, Example XI and accompanying remark: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2312.14051
https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14051 — abstract, version history, and journal reference J. Symbolic Comput. 130 (2025), 102421.
Local Mathlib sources: Mathlib/Data/Nat/Choose/Central.lean; Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Pochhammer.lean; Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/Defs.lean and ENNReal.lean.
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. The `research solved` tag agrees with Au's proof. Lean checks confirmed real rather than natural-number division, the central-binomial definition, positive denominators, and initial summands 1 and 259/8192. The reviewed file was not modified.
